verdict.rationale: Fellow documents its own MCP Server for asking an AI assistant natural-language questions about your meetings, scoped to data the user can access. The pricing page also lists an "Ask Fellow" feature, and transcripts are searchable. However, the conversational answering runs through third-party chatbots via the connector, and nothing documents source-cited answers or querying the full meeting history from inside Fellow. missing for 10: documentation that answers include sources/citations, a described native in-product Q&A experience (Ask Fellow is only a pricing line item), explicit whole-history cross-meeting coverage, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can ask questions in natural language across my whole meeting history ("what did we decide about pricing?") and get answers with sources

citations.quote: Fellow's Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server allows you to ask your AI Assistant about your meetings, without needing to write any code.
Your favorite AI chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now tap directly into your meeting recaps, notes, and action items
The MCP Server only gives users access to the data they already have access to within Fellow.
Every conversation becomes searchable through a full transcript, giving your team instant access to past context whenever they need it.
